checks: For each fiber the fixed-normal margin velocity is w·(x−y)+βz. Divide the old margin and perturbing margin by the same positive ‖u‖ so the fixed-body derivative uses unit normal. At proper A and K sections the derivative is signed, and on the zero-capture B side it is the positive-part integral. An empty or surface-null trace has derivative zero.

The assumption gives nonnegative right derivative for every fixed perturbation, since the normal remains nonzero for sufficiently small positive sizes and the cap still contains the mark on its boundary.
The test w=0, β=1 gives −t+M≥0 and forces a genuine positive-area supporting facet.

The A and B cutting levels average to the K cutting level. Thus midpoint compatibility yields the section inclusion. Translate the three parallel cutting planes consistently into u⊥ and apply Brunn–Minkowski in positive dimension d−1.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use only the single fixed-body slice computation in its proof for an arbitrary affine increment. Proper sections contribute a signed integral and empty-side supporting sections a positive-part integral; no two-mark or global minimizing hypothesis is used.

overlap.comparison: Its fixed-fiber derivative is used exactly. Its stated flux inequality has two distinct minimizing marks and different terms, whereas the present one-mark compatible-chain area bound follows from a base-only velocity and section Brunn–Minkowski.

Its planar proof obtains the corresponding rowwise first variation at a global actual-depth minimizer among three specified caps. The present statement is dimension-independent and assumes only one fixed-mark local minimum.
Its Brunn–Minkowski result assumes equality for captured d-dimensional positive-volume pieces at a global minimizing cap. This result concerns cutting sections opposite a zero-capture endpoint.
